text:
ash: quick question — we're planning the customer cutover from shared NAT -> per-tenant egress IPs behind private endpoints. what's the minimal-risk sequence for control-plane split + endpoint migration?

lena: +1 on pinning a clear sequence. my sketch: 1) enable private control plane in read-only for target tenants 2) stand up per-tenant endpoints (no traffic) 3) run connectivity probes + conntrack draining tests 4) flip a traffic router flag (5-10% canary) 5) escalate to 100% with rollback hooks. keep metrics on conn failures, latency, and SNAT slot usage.

max: main risk is long-lived TCP and DB sessions. SNAT->DNAT switch can break existing conntracks. plan for 2 things: short app-level graceful reconnect OR TCP proxy layer that reoriginates connections. if apps can't tolerate reconnects, do a staged drain using conntrack entries clearing on old path after new path has stable keepalives.

raj: also watch IP preservation for webhook providers — some partners whitelist IPs. we need a plan for a stable egress IP during transition (eg: advertise a temp proxy IP or support both IPs for a grace window).

ash: @lena re: step 2, when endpoints are "no traffic" do you mean route table config only, or also endpoint NATs allocated?

lena: both allocated. allocate IPs and push endpoint configs but keep route advertisement disabled. CI probe will target the endpoint IP directly (bypass router) to validate TLS, KMS access, etc. then enable routing at canary percentage.

max: small note on conntrack: on Linux conntrack entries can persist for minutes. you can accelerate by `conntrack -D -s <old-egress-ip>` but do that only for a canary subset. scripts should use `ss -tnp` + `conntrack -L` to map flows before deletion.

raj: snippet for canary toggle (pseudo-bash):

```bash
# mark 10% of live tenants to new-egress via sharding key
TENANTS=$(./list-tenants | shuf | head -n $(( $(./list-tenants | wc -l) / 10 )))
for t in $TENANTS; do
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://controlplane/tenants/$t/routing -d '{"egress":"per-tenant"}'
done
```

ash: what about DNS TTLs? some customers have 300s TTLs so we can't rely on DNS alone for quick rollback.

lena: agreed. don't use DNS as the only lever. use our router flags and iptables level routing so we can flip instantly. set an expectation with support that some endpoints may need 1-5 min reconnects.

max: if you need near-zero reconnects, we should enable our TCP bounce/proxy for the canary. it keeps client-facing 4-tuple and reestablishes server side. costly but safe.

raj: fallback checklist (short):
- revert router flag to old path
- recreate any conntrack entries if you deleted (or restart proxy to accept old flows)
- re-advertise shared egress IP if you moved it
- run smoke tests for webhooks and DB sessions
- notify customers in slack/email if they hit whitelist issues

ash: does private CP separation affect how we coordinate cert rotation for endpoints?

lena: yes. private CP rollout needs cert sync window: issue new certs, distribute to endpoints, validate chain, then switch active cert. one small gotcha: if we rotate certs during canary, the old control plane should still accept the old cert until all endpoints confirm.

max: monitoring to wire up: per-tenant connection resets, SNAT slot consumption, TCP proxy error rates, TLS handshake failures, and egress bytes/bps per IP. also alert on sudden spike in `ESTABLISHED->CLOSE-WAIT` transitions.

raj: on rollback velocity: we need automated runbook steps in the router service. manual flip must be <30s but allow full system propagation window of 3-5m for conntrack quiescence.

deploy-bot: scheduled cutover window created for 2025-11-04 02:00-04:00 UTC. runbook: https://our.internal/runbooks/egress-cutover

sre-bot: reminder — create perf test traffic shaping so canary tenants get representative load. also tag metrics with `cutover_group` label.

ash: thanks everyone. i'll draft a small RFC with the sequence, canary script, and rollback checklist, and post here for sign-off. :thumbsup:

lena: thanks — add a short test that simulates partner whitelist — test should fetch from the new egress IP and validate a mock partner ACL response.

max: and add conntrack-inspect logs to the canary dashboards (sample query):
`sum(rate(conntrack_deleted_total[1m])) by (tenant)`

raj: if we can, add an observational test that leaves 1% of traffic on old path for 24h to catch weird edge cases before full cutover.

ash: noted. drafting now.
